commits.message:
fix(drafts,parsing): reclassify actually re-parses; fix title generation; fix pipe-delimited subjects

Traced from one message ID the user asked me to check (a real production
email: "Senior SAP ERP Developer | Remote |"). Following it uncovered
four separate, real bugs, each confirmed against production data before
being fixed.

1. reclassify_draft_object() only flipped the draft_type column
   (app/drafts/service.py). This specific email had been misclassified
   as document_kind="resume" at intake (a genuine job posting, wrong
   guess), so it was created as draft_consultant_profile with an empty
   email_parsing.records[] -- parse_email_business_records correctly
   refuses to extract job/hotlist fields from a document_kind it wasn't
   given (see its own "unsupported_email_document_kind" warning). A
   reviewer caught the misclassification and reclassified it to
   draft_job_requirement via the "Mark as..." button -- which used to
   just relabel it, leaving the same empty records[] behind. The draft
   showed as a job requirement in the list with zero actual parsed
   fields: nothing a reviewer could publish, and the correction looked
   successful while silently accomplishing nothing.

   Checked how widespread this was: only this one real draft is
   affected. (Also found and will separately flag 100 more drafts with
   empty records[] -- those are stale test-script fixtures from earlier
   test runs against this database, same-second timestamp cluster,
   synthetic generic_api/telegram/whatsapp source_message_ids -- not a
   live bug, just junk data worth deleting.)

   Fix: reclassify_draft_object now re-runs the real deterministic
   parser (+ LLM fallback, matching real intake exactly) against the
   draft's own stored text whenever the correction target is one of the
   two kinds with a dedicated business parser (job_description/
   hotlist), updating structured_data.email_parsing, confidence,
   requires_review, and title together. Skipped for non-email-channel
   drafts (no raw email text to re-run a parser against) and for
   corrections into types with no business parser (profile/vendor-list/
   channel-note) -- those stay a plain label flip, as before.

2. _title_from_payload's job_title lookup (payload.get("job_title")) was
   checking a key that no real email-channel draft has ever had --
   create_draft_object's actual callers (app/channels/service.py) only
   ever pass payload={"text", "document_kind", "structured_data"}, never
   a bare top-level "job_title". The real value lives at payload[
   "structured_data"]["email_parsing"]["records"][0]["job_title"]. This
   meant every job-requirement draft ever created got the generic "Draft
   Job Requirement" title with no exceptions -- confirmed against
   production: every single one of 105 recent job-requirement drafts has
   this exact title, regardless of what the actual posting was for. The
   review list has been effectively unscannable (every row identical)
   since the review UI existed. Added _first_email_record_field() and
   wired it into both the job-requirement and hotlist title paths (the
   latter gets the single consultant's name, or "Hotlist — N
   consultants" for multi-consultant hotlists, instead of always "Draft
   Hotlist"). Takes effect immediately for every new draft; existing
   drafts keep their stored title unless reclassified (not backfilled --
   flagging this as a call for the user rather than mass-editing titles
   on drafts already sitting in the queue).

3. extract_probable_title() (app/understanding/parsers/basic.py), the
   subject-line title fallback, had no terminator for "|" in its regex
   -- the match failed the instant it hit a pipe character (not in the
   allowed [A-Za-z0-9 .+#/-] class), with none of the existing
   terminator alternatives (" with"/" having"/" for"/" -"/","/end)
   matching at that position either. "Senior SAP ERP Developer | Remote
   |" -- and this is not a one-off: checked real subjects in production
   and found "Urgent Need Python Full Stack Developer || 2 Broadway -
   MTA Headquarters Hybrid || f2F Interview" and "Senior IT Project
   Manager / Application Transition Lead || Remote || 15+ Years" using
   the identical "Title | ..." / "Title || ... || ..." shape. All three
   returned no title at all before this fix. Added "|"/"||" as a
   terminator alongside the existing ones; verified against all three
   real subjects.

New coverage: hermes-850-self-learning-classification-check.py gains
test_reclassify_reparses_email_content_into_the_corrected_kind (the
exact bug, using the real production email's text) and
test_reclassify_reparse_skipped_for_non_email_channel.
hermes-850-email-parsing-check.py gains
test_pipe_delimited_subject_still_yields_a_title. Full regression suite
(18 checks) green against a freshly built image and freshly reset
schema.
